_comment: L-6 · pre-authored lobby moments for Unit 1, Days 1–5, keyed by lesson day. Source: Claude Design 'Lobby Launcher' prototype (2026-09-03). `blocks` names the lobbyReady block types the moment runs on; `debrief` is the Reporter question; `then` is the teacher's next move; `surface` describes what students see. Referenced by day, never copied into block copy (C-2).

moments.title: Notice & Wonder on the NASA briefing
moments.prompt: What did you NOTICE in the briefing? What do you WONDER? 3 notices, 5+ wonders — the Recorder captures them.
moments.debrief: Which of our wonders are physics questions — and which unit will answer them?
moments.then: Tap wonders on the board to sort them into How fast · Where · When · How big · What is it · Can we stop it. Save the board — you'll point back at it in May.
moments.surface: Two columns · NOTICE (3) · WONDER (5+) · one line each, Recorder types, everyone can add

moments.title: Sort the class's wonders
moments.prompt: Drag your group's wonders into the six puzzle questions. Argue about the ones that fit two.
moments.debrief: Which bucket got the most? What does that say about what we care about?
moments.then: Reveal the seven unit titles — the year already has a structure.
moments.surface: Six drop zones · your group's wonder cards · drag to sort

moments.title: One question you really want answered
moments.prompt: Individually: write ONE question about the asteroid you want answered this year. Then agree on your group's top one.
moments.debrief: Reporters: read your group's top question aloud.
moments.then: Read the individual ones tonight — physics vs. social, both valid.
moments.surface: One line · individual · then group vote

2.title: How do we talk about motion?

moments.title: Door to desk and back — how far?
moments.prompt: A student walks from the door to their desk and back. How far did they walk? Some of you said "twice the distance", some said "zero". Can both be right?
moments.debrief: Two right answers — so what are we actually measuring?
moments.then: Name it: DISTANCE (path) vs. DISPLACEMENT (change in position). Vocab goes on the board.
moments.surface: "Both can be right because ___ measures ___ and ___ measures ___."

moments.title: Walk 5 N · 3 E · 5 S
moments.prompt: Walk the path as a group. Sketch it on the grid. Record your DISTANCE walked and your DISPLACEMENT from start — in steps.
moments.debrief: Who's surprised the two numbers are so different?
moments.then: Ask a Skeptic: could displacement ever be bigger than distance?
moments.surface: Graph-paper sketch pad · table: distance / displacement / direction

moments.title: 1 million km — does direction matter?
moments.prompt: If 2026-XJ moves 1 million km, does it MATTER which direction? Convince your group with the map.
moments.debrief: Why can't NASA just report "distance traveled"?
moments.then: The sentence to own by Day 5: "We need displacement, not distance, because the asteroid has DIRECTION."
moments.surface: 2D map · Earth · asteroid position · drag the 1M km arrow

moments.title: Two cars, Fitchburg → Worcester
moments.prompt: One takes 1 hour, one takes 2. Are they moving the same way? Defend it.
moments.then: Build speed and velocity definitions from their words.
moments.surface: "They are / aren't moving the same way because ___."

moments.title: How fast is 8,500 m/s, really?
moments.prompt: 2026-XJ moves at 8,500 m/s. Convert to km/h. Then to mph. Which everyday thing comes closest?
moments.debrief: Faster than anything you've ridden in — by how much?
moments.then: Spoiler: ~30,600 km/h, ~19,000 mph. Way faster than any plane.

moments.title: A graph is a claim — falsify it
moments.prompt: Pick one graph from Match-the-Graph. Tell its story (start, direction, speed). Then name ONE motion that would prove it false.
moments.debrief: Reporters: what motion would prove your graph WRONG?
moments.then: Park on the flat line: high but still. This is the misconception 41% hit last year.
moments.surface: "This graph claims the object ___. It would be wrong if ___." + sketch

moments.title: Same motion, v–t instead of x–t
moments.prompt: Here are yesterday's three position–time graphs. Sketch the velocity–time graph for each. Agree before you submit.
moments.debrief: Constant velocity on x–t is a tilted line. On v–t it's ___?
moments.then: Key insight: horizontal on v–t = constant velocity; tilted = changing (preview of acceleration).
moments.surface: Three mini graph pads · x–t reference above each

moments.title: Decompose 8,500 m/s at 15°
moments.prompt: 2026-XJ moves at 8,500 m/s, 15° from the Earth line. Draw the vector on graph paper, then find the toward-Earth and perpendicular components.
moments.debrief: Which component decides IF it hits? Which decides WHERE it is when it gets here?
moments.then: Visual first, trig second. Recipe card: adjacent → cos, opposite → sin.

moments.title: Why components separately?
moments.prompt: Why does it matter that we calculate the components of the asteroid's velocity separately?
moments.debrief: Toward-Earth tells us ___; perpendicular tells us ___.
moments.then: Watch for students who can compute cos/sin but can't say why.
moments.surface: One or two sentences · group answer

moments.title: Where is 2026-XJ in 6 months?
moments.prompt: Current distance 1.2 × 10⁸ km. Toward-Earth velocity 8,210 m/s. Six months ≈ 1.6 × 10⁷ s. Assume constant velocity. How far from Earth will it be?
moments.debrief: How many groups landed near 0.9 × 10⁸ km? What went wrong for the others?
moments.then: Almost always km↔m. The block converts automatically and shows the rule — make groups say it aloud.

moments.title: How sure are we? Draw the window
moments.prompt: Position is known ±50,000 km; velocity ±200 m/s. Recompute the prediction at both extremes and sketch the window of possible positions.
moments.debrief: Is uncertainty "guessing"? What is it, then?
moments.then: Name the bigger truth: the window is really wider because we assumed constant velocity. That's Unit 2.

moments.title: Why a window, not a point?
moments.prompt: In your own words: why does our prediction have a window of possible positions instead of one exact location?
moments.debrief: Data has noise. Noise propagates. Say it back to me.
moments.then: Foreshadow Days 21–22: you'll do this alone with new data.
moments.surface: One or two sentences · then rate yourself 1–3 on R3
